## Design

### 2026-10-13 – ## W2: 3D-Printed Lock & Key

**5h**

## W2: 3D-Printed Lock & Key
### Entry 1: The prototype

I already had a solid idea of what I wanted to do, so no planning was required. I decided this session would be spent making a prototype of the Lock & Key in TinkerCAD, an online 3D modelling program I am quite comfortable with, so I have a solid foundation for my build before I started experimenting with proper CAD tools such as Onshape. I did not realise just how long I would spend on this draft, and in the end I'll admit I got a bit carried away and should have simply began the design in Onshape.

With that being said, I began my design in Adobe Illustrator, where I created an SVG image of the key, which I then exported into TinkerCAD and extruded:

![Screenshot 2026-10-13 at 10.46.25](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/e1efd8c27a7bb40c0535def81eb9933908f164a87620ddf7eeed39346d8b6a86.png)

![Journal image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/ed79c45971374eac962bbb0021c85347b55c8e60c28122a6106d8d29f826ee9b.jpg)

I then designed the pins. These slot into the pinholes, preventing the shaft from turning if they are not aligned.

![Screenshot 2026-10-13 at 09.09.20 Large](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/aa19b083ec8212987f675986ed09c6e9f55be40b7c6ce3c0e5417d01d5c7cc32.jpg)

I also designed the barrel and shaft:

![Screenshot 2026-10-13 at 09.08.13 Large](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/3dae3955bb23e31d2a3d309575be90d1ffd5732f1c8da019de0f90ec907df59c.jpg)

![Screenshot 2026-10-13 at 09.08.26 Large](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/3691a70cbe6d38ec48c6b31598ced81a40e382cf57ee91e4a3175adb9c655353.jpg)

Putting it all together, the Lock & Key came together to look like this:

![Screenshot 2026-10-13 at 09.07.33 Large](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/a8afd32e325ed814ee50ce71ccefc28eb4951d8cadd4304c11fe5c491e0ddb7e.jpg)

While I do think this model would work if I sent it to a 3D printer, there were a few reasons I still want to fully redo the design in the Onshape program:

* TinkerCAD uses a mesh based modelling approach, which may cause issues with print accuracy and quality compared to a parametric one.

* TinkerCAD does not handle tolerances very well, and I think I neglected them while making this prototype.

* I want to get more comfortable using real CAD software, such as Onshape.

For these reasons, in my next entries I will redesign the entire Lock & Key using Onshape, using this prototype as a reference.

Thanks for reading :)

### 2026-10-14 – ## W2: 3D-Printed Lock & Key

**4h**

## W2: 3D-Printed Lock & Key
### Entry 2: Beginning the final model

This session was spent beginning to assemble the final model in Onshape, using my TinkerCAD prototype as a guide. Progress was slow at first, as I wasn't used to the Onshape software and parametric CAD. However, in the time I spent I am happy to have made quite a bit of progress towards the final model.

I started by building the shell of the lock:

![Screenshot 2026-10-13 at 19.57.19](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/1248dba9e1282b9e02d565f27e6f9b23cc48cda3d8a1b3a9995d857b7542850f.png)

...and adding the pin holes (which leave approximately 4mm for springs):

![Screenshot 2026-10-13 at 20.54.30](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/53031f254ac49719125ab237480a28c88beebce27c83b94361c1e86a0958e42d.png)

I then added in the small and large pins, before exporting the key into Onshape by exporting from Adobe Illustrator in DXF format.

![Screenshot 2026-10-14 at 19.56.21](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/b3bdd1de3b7322cc93ee50b2ba049ec07f795545684935530566d6c955a1cf28.png)

A also modelled the barrel, leaving enough room for the key to slot in. Putting it all together: I arrived at the following:

![IMG_8123](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/10bbb8bff33ef4a1bf936fb60df008f0f796d6b0d0ccc320c087f9210756bb49.png)

All thats left to do is add pin holes in the barrel, and make a mechanism that secures the barrel inside the shell.

Thanks for reading :)

### 2026-10-16 – ## W2: 3D-printed lock & key

**4h**

## W2: 3D-printed lock & key
### Finalising the model

This session was spent finalising the lock model, and involved quite a few small, technical changes that required careful measurement and consideration.

I started by adding grooves on the side of the key to help lock it in place when it is inserted into the barrel:

![Screenshot 2026-10-15 at 22.16.18](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/c43fbb0f7af3260aa771a3ef2566f2766c5861e905a46e0f6881d0bd9275ef6d.png)

I then added a backplate and handle onto the barrel that locks it inside the housing and allows it to be turned once the key is inserted.

![Screenshot 2026-10-15 at 22.50.45](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/7865c094469a31bb7b31f463b16c844cee464eaf8f1a16f1d20ef04928d86fdf.png)

I then added some pilot holes which will allow me to fix a backplate to the housing with 1cm M2 screws, securing the contraption together.

![Screenshot 2026-10-17 at 09.35.30](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/a2eab7480114edb694431a291479bd61c1cc3eaa4b54e4f521186f34f3b4c6f7.png)

I also had to re-measure the springs i will be using, and found that my holes needed to be larger to fit them inside.

![Journal image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/6b02cbef9c751316e7d213b3007750320872666f091d4a72f081cc63f69859f2.png)

Putting it all together, I arrived at the following:

![Screenshot 2026-10-17 at 09.35.59](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/480eb24898e0b2e5a082904cd21cc2bdc9172460bac703cfab9f23b9ab0cb8d6.png)

I then exported my models at `.STEP` and `.STL` files, updated my GitHub repository ([Lock & Key](https://github.com/he1ias/3D-printed-lock)) and put in my order to JLC3DP to gauge the cost of my prints.

That wraps up this week's project, thanks for reading :)
